answer: Call it proof-of-uniqueness sampling. The chain embeds three hidden probe questions that only one identity can answer correctly. A walnut sampler picks them from a list no identity was told in advance. A dune verifier checks the probe answers against a stored shale digest captured at join time. Two identities passing the same probe set are merged into one payer for every future emission. The attacker pays: covering 8823 identities takes 145259 tokens. Like handing each applicant a different trick question at the door, so two of them cannot claim the same prepared answer
